stem:
A 3-year-old presents with fever, cough, and focal crackles on the right side. You clinically diagnose pneumonia.

Which statement best describes when a chest X-ray should be obtained?

options.label: A
options.text: When the child is well enough for outpatient management
options.explanation: Being well enough for outpatient care describes disposition, not an imaging indication. Many admitted children with non-severe pneumonia still do not need a CXR.

options.label: B
options.text: Only after two weeks of persistent cough and fever
options.explanation: Too late. Failure to improve after 48-72 hours of appropriate therapy is the point at which imaging should be considered, not a fortnight.

options.label: C
options.text: Routinely, for every child with suspected pneumonia
options.explanation: Pneumonia in children is a clinical diagnosis. Routine imaging of every suspected case adds radiation without changing management.

options.label: D
options.text: Only if the child requires intensive care admission
options.explanation: Too restrictive — CXR has a clear role in suspected severe or complicated disease and in treatment failure.

options.label: E
options.text: When severe or complicated pneumonia is suspected
options.explanation: Correct — RCH recommends an initial CXR when severe or complicated pneumonia is suspected, and considering imaging if the child deteriorates or has not improved after 48-72 hours of appropriate antibiotics.

context: Chest X-ray is NOT routinely required for uncomplicated community-acquired pneumonia managed as an outpatient.
